name: E2E the passwordless front door
description: Expose the RESONANCE_FAKES fake-mail transport via peekLoginCode + a flag-gated GET /api/test/last-otp route; poll it with expect.poll for the OTP; fill the 'Digit N of 6' cells. Assert only settled state (getByRole/toBeVisible/toHaveURL), never mid-stream tokens.

name: Isolated E2E harness (ADR-0018 §4) replaces the RESONANCE_FAKES flag
description: The full-flow onboarding Playwright E2E stays deterministic + credential-free via ONE explicit, prod-hard-guarded harness — the sanctioned ADR-0018 §4 exception — NOT a general fakes flag or per-seam runtime branch. apps/web/lib/e2e-harness.ts is the SINGLE place a fake is selected: export const E2E_HARNESS = process.env.E2E_HARNESS === '1' && process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'. It exposes harnessModel(), harnessEmbedder() (=@resonance/ai/test createFakeEmbedder), and a MODULE-SINGLETON harnessMail() (=@resonance/auth/testing createFakeMail().port — one instance so the auth handler's send and peekLoginCode observe the same globalThis-registered codes buffer). @resonance/* packages stay live-by-default and UNTOUCHED. Composition roots each consult it with a single 'E2E_HARNESS ? harness : live' ternary at the shell boundary: interview/route.ts + actions.ts generateDraft (RunInput.model), commitProfile (embedder), and a new apps/web/lib/auth.ts getWebAuth() that builds an isolated createAuth({db:createDb(),mail:harnessMail()}) instance for the [...all] mount. getSession keeps using live getAuth() — correct because harness auth shares the same secret+DB (sessions validate) and no live mail send occurs. The deleted fake-of-a-fake is restored as @resonance/ai/test createFakeOnboardingModel — ONE MockLanguageModelV3 serving BOTH doStream (canned interview line) and doGenerate (forced proposeProfile tool-call, bio derived from the doGenerate prompt's first user turn) since harnessModel() is used at both roots. playwright.config webServer sets env {E2E_HARNESS:'1', BETTER_AUTH_SECRET:<fixed throwaway>} — needed because next dev is NODE_ENV=development where the auth-secret dev fallback is off. last-otp route + spec re-pointed to E2E_HARNESS; zero functional RESONANCE_FAKES refs remain. Boundary lint only blocks @resonance/*/src|dist, so /test + /testing subpaths and ai/test are fine to import from apps/web; next build keeps the test-util import server-side.

The app-capture loop (apps/web/scripts/capture-app-manifest.mjs, E2E_HARNESS=1) hit two gotchas: (1) GET /api/test/last-otp returns null under next dev because the readback route and the auth mount evaluate SEPARATE @resonance/auth/testing module instances, so the peek registry the route reads is not the one the mount fake registered into; (2) the first authed navigation after a code change cold-recompiles the route in next dev and times out.
resolution: Read the OTP from the dev server log line [fake-mail] login code for EMAIL: CODE instead of the /api/test/last-otp route. Warm-retry the capture once after a code change (the cold recompile succeeds on the second run; CSS hot-reload itself works).

description: The capture/verify loop's next-dev harness can corrupt its .next cache: auth routes 500 with 'Cannot find module ./vendor-chunks/@better-auth+core...js' (require stack through apps/web/.next/server/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.js), so capture-app-manifest fails at signup->verify (no nav) even though E2E_HARNESS is still on (fake-mail log lines still print). Not a code bug — a stale webpack chunk reference.
resolution: Kill the server on :3001, rm -rf apps/web/.next, restart E2E_HARNESS=1 PORT=3001 pnpm --dir apps/web dev, warm the routes (curl), then re-run the capture. Point SERVER_LOG at the fresh dev log for OTP read-back.

name: Deterministic discovery ranking in Playwright via the harness's text-hash embedder
description: Ranked-search E2E does not need to mock the app. Under E2E_HARNESS=1 apps/web/lib/e2e-harness.ts discoveryEmbedder() resolves createFakeEmbedder(), a PURE text-derived hash. So a fixture profile whose embedded content is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the query text scores cosine 1.0 and is rank 1 by construction; content + a suffix ranks just below. apps/web/e2e/lib/discovery-fixtures.ts seeds three profiles this way (top, second, draft) and the spec asserts only the RELATIVE order of its own two rows, so the ~20 pre-existing dev-DB profiles and other Playwright workers' fixtures interleave harmlessly. The draft fixture is embedded from the SAME text as the top row on purpose: a regression in the status='ready' filter ranks it FIRST rather than failing quietly. Fixtures carry a per-worker run id (module scope is per worker process, so a beforeAll-generated id is naturally unique) and are deleted in afterAll. Inserts/deletes go through db.$client — the raw Neon tagged template Drizzle exposes — so apps/web needs no drizzle-orm dependency for fixtures. process.loadEnvFile('.env.local') gives the Playwright runner DATABASE_URL, which next dev loads for itself but the test process does not inherit.

onboarding-creator.spec.ts (and any Playwright spec that signs in through /signup) intermittently dies at the OTP poll with 'Matcher error: received value must be a string' — /api/test/last-otp answers {"otp":null} forever. NOT a module-scope divergence (the buffer IS globalThis-pinned) and NOT a timeout: harnessMailOverride() in apps/web/lib/e2e-harness.ts awaits a dynamic import BETWEEN its !store[KEY] guard and its assignment. The signup form fires TWO Better Auth calls in parallel (signIn.magicLink + emailOtp.sendVerificationOtp), so on a COLD server both pass the guard, both build a fake, and both call observeLoginCodes(): one fake wins store[HARNESS_MAIL_KEY] (the port the auth mount sends through), the other wins the process-wide observation slot peekLoginCode reads. Codes land in an array nothing reads. Symptom is timing-dependent — it passes once the server is warm, which is why it looks flaky.
resolution: Diagnose by contrast, not by staring: a SINGLE direct POST to /api/auth/email-otp/send-verification-otp always works; only the browser's parallel pair fails. Mitigate test-side with ONE warm auth request (await request.get('/api/auth/get-session')) before driving /signup — 3/3 green after. Real fix (resonance-86dd): pin the PROMISE, not the resolved port, to globalThis so concurrent callers await the same construction; same shape applies to getWebAuth()'s store[HARNESS_AUTH_KEY] ??= createAuth(...).

description: Playwright fixture cleanup written as a finally inside the test body silently leaks rows: a test TIMEOUT aborts the body at its current await, so the finally never runs. Reproduced accidentally while mutation-testing the interests spec - the timed-out run left its fixture behind and poisoned the next run, which is the mechanism behind the leaked-fixture bug that had previously been mis-diagnosed as un-scoped fixture query text.
resolution: Put fixture and account cleanup in test.afterEach (or afterAll), which Playwright still runs after a timeout and gives its own time budget. Never a finally inside the test body. Where a fixture cannot be run-scoped, add a stale-sibling sweep at seed time plus an in-run pollution check that names the cause.

description: The creator onboarding E2E signed up an account and committed a creator profile on every run and deleted neither, publishing one more ranked creator into the shared dev database each time. It reached 70 of 80 creator profiles named New Creator, crowding real creators off the first page of every discovery search - visible in a screenshot of the personalized discover surface, where seven of eight rows were test debris. Deleting the user is not enough on its own: the embeddings table has no foreign key to anything (source_id is plain text holding both profile uuids and member ids), so the cascade removes the profile but strands its vector.
resolution: Give every spec that signs up an account an afterEach that deletes it, and make the delete helper remove BOTH embedding kinds (source_type interest keyed by user id, and source_type creator_profile keyed by the profile uuid) before deleting the user, while the join target still exists. Verify by measurement, not assertion: count rows before and after a full run and require them unchanged.

name: exact-match fixture for assertable vector ranking
description: To assert a RANKING rather than merely that rows came back, seed a fixture whose embedded content is byte-identical to what the product will embed for the query side. Under the E2E harness both sides run through the deterministic text-hash fake embedder, so identical text yields cosine similarity 1.0 - the maximum - and the fixture must therefore rank first. Derive the text the same way the product does rather than hardcoding it (for member interests: the selected topic LABELS, in taxonomy sort order, joined with a comma and a space), so the test fails if the two sides ever stop being built to be compared. Caveat: content dictated by shared data cannot be run-scoped, so two simultaneous runs tie at 1.0 - pair it with a pollution check that reports that cause explicitly instead of failing as an ordering bug.
